page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6455B processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory provision comprises 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The processor incorporates modern vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512 and AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) along with 60 MB of Level 3 cache. Network performance features a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps. The instance includes zero GPUs and no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent storage operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate high compute and memory capabilities. The instance registers top-tier Geekbench results with a single-core score of 2,262.0 and a multi-core score of 21,445.0. Stress-ng multi-core testing reached 69,189.84 points, while PassMark database operations achieved 33,888.6 points, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Redis throughput reached 78.59 million SET operations per second, supported by uncached memory read bandwidth of 244.57 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 105.85 GB/sec. Onboard AMX instructions facilitate capable CPU-based LLM inference, reaching 300.35 tokens per second for prompt processing on 7B models and 39.13 tokens per second on 70B models.

The r7iz.16xlarge instance balances high single-core frequencies with large memory capacity, offering strong efficiency for enterprise memory-intensive applications. Because the instance lacks ephemeral NVMe drives, storage architectures must rely completely on external elastic storage volumes, introducing architectural considerations for IOPS-bound operations. It is well-matched for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics platforms, enterprise relational database systems, and CPU-driven machine learning inference pipelines.
